To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the production cross sections of neutron-rich nuclei close to the drip line are correlated with the Qg values and can be interpreted in terms of shell effects in these nuclei.
the production cross sections from 76 Ge and 82 Se fragmentation show systematic trends with the shell model that predicts subshell closures for the isotopes 68 Cr and 72 Mn, respectively.
shell effects in the neutron-rich region of the nuclear chart can be deduced from production cross sections from fragmentation of a 139 MeV/ 82 Se beam.

the production of exotic nuclei in the vicinity of the neutron drip-line.
the production cross sections of nuclei close to the drip line and their dependence on shell effects.
the production of exotic neutron-rich nuclei in the vicinity of the drip-line and their properties, which can be studied with a variety of experimental techniques.

shell effects in neutron-deficient nuclei are stronger than in their neutron-rich isotopes.
